zh.title: 賽斯納441包機於阿拉斯加軍用雷達站附近墜毀機上8人全數罹難
zh.summary: Security Aviation賽斯納441包機於阿拉斯加墜毀，機上8人罹難。
body: 一架由安克拉治 Security Aviation 營運的賽斯納 441 Conquest II（Cessna 441 Conquest II）雙引擎渦輪螺旋槳包機，於 2026 年 8 月 20 日在地頭時間約 12 時 15 分，於阿拉斯加州西部紐恩漢角長程雷達站機場（Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport）西側陸地上墜毀。美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）與救援人員證實，機上包含兩名機師與六名乘客在內共八人全部罹難，現場無人倖存。
根據報導，該架客機當天自泰德·史蒂文斯安克拉治國際機場（ANC）起飛，並由美國陸軍工兵部隊（US Army Corps of Engineers）承包租用。美國陸軍工兵部隊證實，罹難者中有兩名為該機構之員工，但尚未公開其姓名或此次出差之目的。涉事航空器在美國聯邦航空總署的登記編號為 N128EZ，製造年份為 1979 年。
事發地點紐恩漢角長程雷達站機場為美國空軍轄下的私人跑道，位於安克拉治以西約 450 英里處，專門用於支援監測阿拉斯加周邊空域的長程雷達站。該機場設有單一碎石跑道，長度約 3,945 英尺，座落於山坡上且兩端高差超過 300 英尺。航情資訊警告該跑道兩側均有高聳地形，重飛成功機率極低。相關單位回報，事故發生當時該區域出現濃霧天氣。
美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）已針對此起墜機事故展開調查，並由美國聯邦航空總署及其他地方與聯邦機構協助辦理。調查人員目前尚未公佈殘骸狀況、航空器最終飛行軌跡或任何潛在的機械異常原因。阿拉斯加指揮部指揮官羅伯特·戴維斯（Lt. Gen. Robert Davis）發表聲明表達哀悼，並強調機上所有人員皆為在極具挑戰環境中執行關鍵任務的專業人士。

en.title: Cessna 441 Charter Crash Near Alaska Military Radar Site Kills All Eight On Board
en.summary: Security Aviation Cessna 441 crashed in western Alaska on August 20, killing all eight people on board.
body: A chartered Cessna 441 Conquest II twin-engine turboprop aircraft crashed on land west of Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport in western Alaska at approximately 12:15 local time on August 20, 2026. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and local emergency rescue teams reached the crash site and confirmed that all eight people on board, comprising two pilots and six passengers, were killed in the accident, with no survivors found.

The aircraft had departed earlier from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC) before traveling toward the remote destination. The flight was chartered by the US Army Corps of Engineers, which confirmed that two of its employees were among those killed. The agency stated it is coordinating closely with local, state, and federal authorities, but has not yet identified the deceased employees or disclosed the specific purpose of their official visit. Federal Aviation Administration registration records indicate that the aircraft, registered as N128EZ, was a 1979 Cessna 441 Conquest II operated by Anchorage-based Security Aviation.

The crash occurred while the aircraft was approaching Cape Newenham LRRS Airport, a private airstrip operated by the US Air Force located approximately 450 miles west of Anchorage. The facility provides access to a remote long-range radar station managed by the Pacific Air Forces Regional Support Center to monitor airspace over Alaska. The airport features a single gravel runway measuring approximately 3,945 feet in length that is situated on a mountain slope, with FAA airport information warning of high terrain and cautioning that a successful go-around is improbable. Fog was also reported in the area at the time of the accident.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is leading the accident investigation with assistance from the FAA and other federal and state agencies. Officials stated that investigators have not yet released information regarding the condition of the aircraft wreckage, its final flight path, or any possible mechanical issues. US Air Force Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of Alaskan Command, expressed condolences, noting that every individual on board was a dedicated professional supporting a vital mission in a challenging operational environment.
